title: W-9 Forms for Delaware C-Corps: How to Complete and Collect Them
summary: W-9 Forms for Delaware C-Corps: How to Complete and Collect Them
body_markdown:
An enterprise customer asks for your startup's W-9 before paying an invoice. At the same time, your accountant asks for W-9s from the contractors your company hired. Both requests concern taxpayer identity, but your company plays a different role in each.


A Delaware C-corp completes its own W-9 as a vendor and collects W-9s as a payer. Keeping those workflows separate prevents founder information from slipping into corporate records.


## Complete your corporation's form


Use the current form and[IRS instructions](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/iw9) . For a standard domestic C-corporation, the key entries are:


- Line 1: the corporation's name as shown on its federal tax return.
- Line 2: a business or disregarded-entity name, if different and applicable.
- Line 3a: the C corporation classification for an entity taxed that way.
- Address: the address where the company should receive tax correspondence.
- Part I: the corporation's EIN, matching the taxpayer name.
- Part II: the required certification, completed by an authorized person as applicable.


Do not use your personal SSN simply because you are the founder or sole shareholder. Avoid replacing the legal entity name with a product name customers recognize. A consistent name-and-EIN pair makes customer onboarding and tax reporting easier.


## Do not guess exemption codes


Some corporations qualify for particular exemptions, but exemptions depend on the payment and the rule involved. Read the instructions before entering an exempt-payee or FATCA code. The fact that a company is a corporation does not make every payment to it exempt from information reporting.


Ask your tax team to approve a company W-9 template once, then maintain a controlled copy. Revisit it when the legal name, address, or tax classification changes.


## Review vendors' forms for consistency


When collecting a W-9, compare the taxpayer details with your vendor record. A sole proprietor may use an individual name on line 1 and a business name on line 2. A disregarded single-member LLC generally identifies its owner on line 1, the LLC on line 2, and the owner's federal classification. An LLC taxed as a corporation or partnership follows different instructions.


“LLC” in an invoice heading is therefore insufficient to decide whether contractor payments require a 1099. If entries conflict, ask the vendor for a corrected form rather than changing their certification yourself.


## Use the appropriate form for foreign payees


W-9 is generally for U.S. persons. A foreign founder does not automatically make a domestic Delaware corporation foreign for this purpose. Conversely, a foreign contractor serving a U.S. startup is not automatically a W-9 payee.


Foreign vendors may require an appropriate W-8 form and a separate review of services, source of income, withholding, and reporting. Route those cases to your tax team before payment.


## Keep the process secure and current


W-9s contain sensitive identifiers. Use a secure collection channel, restrict access, and retain the forms with your vendor tax records. The payer generally keeps the form instead of routinely filing it with the IRS.


Maintain a short queue of missing, inconsistent, or outdated forms. Resolve that queue throughout the year so your startup's year-end reporting can use verified information.
